How to Start a Podcast in 2026: Complete Beginner’s Guide

Podcasting has become one of the fastest-growing ways to share ideas, build a personal brand, and connect with audiences. In 2026, starting a podcast is easier than ever, but creating a professional and engaging show still requires planning and the right setup. Here’s a simple beginner’s guide to help you launch your first podcast.

1. Choose Your Podcast Topic
Start by selecting a topic you are passionate about and knowledgeable in. It could be business, lifestyle, technology, storytelling, interviews, or personal experiences. The key is consistency—choose a niche that allows you to create regular content and attract a specific audience.

2. Plan Your Podcast Format
Decide how your podcast will be structured. Some popular formats include solo episodes, interviews, panel discussions, or storytelling. Planning the format in advance helps keep your episodes organized and engaging for listeners.

3. Get the Right Equipment
Good audio quality is essential for a successful podcast. At minimum, you’ll need a quality microphone, headphones, and recording software. Many creators also choose professional podcast studios to ensure clear sound, proper acoustics, and high-quality video recording for platforms like YouTube.

4. Record and Edit Your Episodes
Record your podcast in a quiet environment to avoid background noise. After recording, edit the audio to remove mistakes, pauses, or noise. Adding intro music and sound effects

We hired this photographer for two preschool events with a fixed rate agreed for both events.
On the morning of the first event, he suddenly demanded ₹500 extra for just 15 additional minutes, which was never discussed during finalization.

Main events were missed, while irrelevant side moments were covered
Videos were blurry
No noise cancellation during speeches and parent testimonials
Overall output was unusable and disappointing
When we shared our feedback, he initially accepted his mistake. We requested to meet before the second event to clearly guide him on what needed coverage. After this, he stopped answering calls and messages.
As the second event date approached, he:
Increased the price to double the committed amount
Refused to meet or discuss
Claimed he was traveling
Asked for advance payment
Said he would only talk 2 days before the event
To cover up his poor work, he started blaming us for mismanagement, which was completely untrue.
Additional concerns:
Very poor song selection in videos
If changes are requested, he claims he is “too busy” to discuss
No studio address provided; asked us to meet on a roadside while taking advance
Claimed to bring an extra photographer, but that person was clearly inexperienced and delivered badly zoomed, awkward photos that looked like low-quality BTS shots
Overall, this was a highly unprofessional and dishonest experience.
Not recommended at all, especially for important events involving children and parents.
